It is comparable to the current development URL flow, not production OTA delivery. - **Where does the device persist state for comparison with the Worker response?** Native preferences through `LynxChannelState`. Bundle bytes remain in the filesystem through `LynxBundleStore`. - **How does the device decide whether to download?** Compare the locally persisted manifest ID with the Worker response’s `manifestSha256`; skip when equal. Also skip manifest IDs recorded in crash history. - **Does the architecture need background fetch?** No. Update discovery/download occurs during launch; activation is immediate or deferred to next open. - **What did “wait for safe boundary” do?** It was a manual host-controlled activation mode. It has been removed from the current architecture. - **How does Hot Updater manage bundles?** It uses a native bundle identity, persistent crash history, update discovery, installation, pending activation, `notifyAppReady`, and automatic recovery when a launch fails before readiness. - **Can Hot Updater code be reused?** Small MIT-licensed primitives and design patterns can be adapted. The full React Native bridge, archive storage service, updater orchestration, and plugin system should not be reused directly. - **How does bsdiff work?** It generates control, diff, and extra streams that reconstruct a new binary from an exact old binary. Hot Updater can generate patches from several prior Hermes bundle bases and falls back to full downloads when no compatible patch exists. - **Can bsdiff technically work with Lynx bundles?** Yes, because it operates on opaque binary data. It should not be implemented until real Lynx bundle pairs show worthwhile compression and the architecture supports exact base identification and full-download fallback. - **Is the architecture production-safe as originally documented?** Not without a readiness watchdog, crash history, staging policy, signing-key rotation/key IDs, and explicit dev-only HMR handling. These are required planning items. - **Should the documentation be gutted to make it simpler?** It should be consolidated, not blindly gutted. Remove confirmed duplicate files and diagrams, but retain a canonical architecture rationale and self-contained PR acceptance contracts. ## Relevant Files - `/Users/phirom/Desktop/expo-lynx/lynx-architecture/README.md` — architecture index and older Mermaid flow; {"path":"/Users/phirom/Desktop/expo-lynx/.hermes/plans/2026-08-28_082147-lynx-miniapp-remote-bundle-architecture.md","content":"# Lynx Mini-App Remote Bundle Architecture Implementation Plan\n\n> **For Hermes:** Use subagent-driven-development skill to implement this plan task-by-task.\n\n**Goal:** Add a production-safe remote Lynx bundle update system to the `expo-lynx` Expo module, with an embedded offline baseline, Cloudflare R2 delivery, signed manifests, launch-time update checks, asset prefetch, two activation modes, and automatic rollback.\n\n**Architecture:** React Native owns durable application state and chooses a feature/channel; native iOS/Android code owns all trust decisions, storage, activation, and rollback before passing verified local bytes to `LynxView`. Cloudflare Workers + D1 provide a signed mutable channel pointer, while R2 stores only immutable content-addressed release manifests, bundles, and sidecar assets. The client renders the current verified local release immediately (or embedded baseline), checks once at launch, then either activates the verified candidate in the same launch or records it for the next launch.\n\n**Tech Stack:** Expo SDK 57 / Expo Modules API, React Native 0.86, TypeScript, Swift + CryptoKit, Kotlin + Android Keystore/JCA, Lynx 4.0, Jest, XCTest, JUnit, Cloudflare Workers, R2, D1, Cloudflare Access.\n\n---\n\n## 1. Scope and production defaults\n\n### In scope\n\n- One Lynx feature (`delivery`) and one active channel per view (`stable` or `beta`).\n- Embedded `static.lynx` plus its sidecar assets as the permanent offline baseline.\n- One launch-time channel check; no timer and no OS background-fetch task.\n- One update transaction at a time.\n- Full prefetch of the bundle and every asset declared in the signed release manifest.\n- Two normal activation modes:\n  - `next-open` — default; stage now, activate at the next app launch.\n  - `on-launch` — activate in the current launch after complete verification.\n- Web-console `force` policy — override `next-open` to current-launch activation after verification. It never bypasses signature, compatibility, crash-history, or fallback checks.\n- Last-known-good rollback after render failure, watchdog timeout, or an unconfirmed prior launch.\n- Server rollback by publishing a newer channel revision that targets an older immutable release.\n- iOS-first implementation with Android parity before production release.\n\n### Explicitly out of scope\n\n- Multi-feature mini-app registry/service.\n- Sparkling as the embed layer.\n- bsdiff/delta patching.\n- Background downloads, timers, silent mid-session swaps, or OS background tasks.\n- Cohorts, per-user targeting, A/B testing, and phased rollout.\n- Custom authentication UI or custom RBAC for the web console; use Cloudflare Access.\n- Hot Updater's plugin system, CLI surface, React wrapper, and archive formats.\n\n### Recommended defaults\n\n- Default activation: `next-open`.\n- A `force` release activates in the current launch only after all files verify.\n- If a forced update fails, keep the current/LKG bundle; do not brick or block the RN shell.\n- Keep at most: active remote release + previous LKG + one pending candidate. Embedded baseline is outside this quota.\n- Private Ed25519 key lives only in a Worker secret; never in D1, R2, source control, or the app.\n- Public keys are embedded in the app as a trust set. A key fetched from the same server is not a trust root.\n\n---\n\n## 2. Canonical architecture\n\n### 2.1 Component diagram\n\n```mermaid\nflowchart TB\n  subgraph APP[Expo / React Native host]\n    RN[Feature screen\\nfeature + channel + initialData]\n    API[ExpoLynxView JS API\\nsource + events + reload]\n    COORD[Native LynxUpdateCoordinator\\nlaunch check + decision + activation]\n    STATE[Native UpdateStateStore\\nUserDefaults / SharedPreferences]\n    STORE[Native BundleStore\\nstaging + ready directories]\n    VIEW[ExpoLynxView\\nverified local URLs only]\n    LYNX[LynxView + local resource resolver]\n    EMBED[Embedded baseline\\nstatic.lynx + assets + manifest]\n\n    RN --> API --> COORD\n    COORD --> STATE\n    COORD --> STORE\n    COORD --> VIEW --> LYNX\n    EMBED --> STORE\n  end\n\n  subgraph CF[Cloudflare]\n    WORKER[Worker API\\nchannel + publish + promote + rollback]\n    D1[(D1\\nreleases + channel revisions + audit)]\n    R2[(R2\\nimmutable manifests + files)]\n    ACCESS[Cloudflare Access\\nadmin console auth]\n    CONSOLE[Minimal web console\\nlist / promote / force / rollback]\n\n    ACCESS --> CONSOLE --> WORKER\n    WORKER --> D1\n    WORKER --> R2\n  end\n\n  COORD -- signed short-lived pointer --> WORKER\n  STORE -- immutable HTTPS objects --> R2\n```\n\n### 2.2 Trust boundary\n\n```text\nReact Native may choose feature/channel/activation preference.\nReact Native may NOT provide executable production URLs.\n\nWorker response\n  -> verify channel-envelope signature with embedded public key\n  -> reject replayed channel revision\n  -> require exact runtimeVersion\n  -> verify release-envelope SHA-256 + signature\n  -> download all declared files to staging\n  -> verify path, byte count, and SHA-256 for every file\n  -> atomic rename staging -> ready/<releaseId>\n  -> only then give local file URLs to LynxView\n```\n\n### 2.3 Local storage layout\n\nUse one canonical metadata store; do not duplicate the active pointer in both a text file and preferences.\n\n```text\n<Application Support>/ExpoLynx/delivery/\n  ready/\n    <releaseId>/\n      release-envelope.json       # exact verified bytes\n      main.lynx.bundle\n      static/...\n  staging/\n    <uuid>/                       # one in-flight transaction; delete on failure\n\nApp bundle:\n  static.lynx\n  static/...\n  embedded-release-envelope.json\n```\n\n`UserDefaults` / `SharedPreferences` owns only metadata:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"channel\": \"stable\",\n  \"lastAcceptedRevision\": 42,\n  \"activeReleaseId\": \"sha256-a\",\n  \"previousLkgReleaseId\": \"sha256-b\",\n  \"pendingReleaseId\": null,\n  \"attemptingReleaseId\": null,\n  \"failedReleaseIds\": [\"sha256-bad\"],\n  \"lastCheckedAt\": \"2026-08-28T01:20:00Z\",\n  \"lastETag\": \"...\"\n}\n```\n\nRules:\n\n- `activeReleaseId` points to the currently confirmed remote release; absent means embedded.\n- `previousLkgReleaseId` is retained until a newer candidate is confirmed.\n- `pendingReleaseId` is a fully verified `next-open` candidate.\n- `attemptingReleaseId` is written synchronously before rendering an unconfirmed candidate.\n- If the next process launch sees `attemptingReleaseId`, the prior attempt never confirmed; add it to `failedReleaseIds`, roll back, then clear it.\n- A failed immutable `releaseId` is never retried. Republishing fixed bytes creates a different ID.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Wire contracts\n\n### 3.1 Signed envelope\n\nAvoid JSON-canonicalization ambiguity by signing exact payload bytes:\n\n```ts\ntype SignedEnvelope = {\n  payload: string;   // base64url(UTF-8 JSON bytes)\n  keyId: string;\n  signature: string; // base64url(Ed25519 signature over decoded payload bytes)\n};\n```\n\n### 3.2 Channel pointer payload\n\n```ts\ntype ChannelPointerPayload = {\n  schemaVersion: 1;\n  feature: 'delivery';\n  channel: 'stable' | 'beta';\n  revision: number;              // monotonic per feature+channel\n  target:\n    | {\n        kind: 'release';\n        releaseId: string;\n        manifestUrl: string;\n        manifestSha256: string;\n      }\n    | { kind: 'keep-current' };\n  activation: 'next-open' | 'on-launch';\n  force: boolean;\n  runtimeVersion: string;\n  issuedAt: string;\n  expiresAt: string;\n};\n```\n\nA rollback increments `revision` and points to an older `releaseId`; clients therefore accept legitimate rollback while rejecting replay of an older channel response.\n\n### 3.3 Release manifest payload\n\n```ts\ntype ReleaseManifestPayload = {\n  schemaVersion: 1;\n  feature: 'delivery';\n  releaseId: string;             // SHA-256 of unsigned payload bytes excluding releaseId, or CI-generated immutable ID\n  displayVersion: string;\n  runtimeVersion: string;        // exact compatibility boundary, Expo Updates style\n  createdAt: string;\n  gitSha?: string;\n  files: Array<{\n    path: string;                // normalized relative path, never absolute / never ..\n    role: 'template' | 'resource';\n    url: string;\n    sha256: string;\n    bytes: number;\n  }>;\n};\n```\n\nExactly one file has `role: 'template'`. Every runtime resource is declared. The client resolves relative paths only inside the selected ready directory.\n\n### 3.4 Public JS API\n\nKeep JS declarative. Native owns update mechanics.\n\n```ts\nexport type LynxSource =\n  | { kind: 'embedded'; feature: 'delivery' }\n  | {\n      kind: 'managed';\n      feature: 'delivery';\n      channel?: 'stable' | 'beta';\n      activation?: 'next-open' | 'on-launch';\n    }\n  | { kind: 'development'; url: string };\n\nexport type ExpoLynxViewProps = {\n  source: LynxSource;\n  initialData?: Record<string, unknown>;\n  onLoadStart?: (event: NativeSyntheticEvent<LynxLoadEvent>) => void;\n  onLoad?: (event: NativeSyntheticEvent<LynxLoadEvent>) => void;\n  onError?: (event: NativeSyntheticEvent<LynxErrorEvent>) => void;\n  onUpdate?: (event: NativeSyntheticEvent<LynxUpdateEvent>) => void;\n};\n```\n\nKeep deprecated `url` for one release cycle in Debug only, with a warning. Release rejects raw URLs natively.\n\n---\n\n## 4. Launch, update, activation, and rollback workflow\n\n### 4.1 End-to-end sequence\n\n```mermaid\nsequenceDiagram\n  autonumber\n  participant App as RN App\n  participant C as Native Coordinator\n  participant S as Local State/Store\n  participant V as LynxView\n  participant W as Cloudflare Worker\n  participant R as R2\n\n  App->>C: mount managed source\n  C->>S: recover unconfirmed attempt\n  alt prior candidate unconfirmed\n    S->>S: failed += attempting; active = previousLkg\n  end\n  C->>S: resolve current local release\n  alt active cached release exists\n    S-->>C: local ready URL\n  else no valid cache\n    S-->>C: embedded baseline URL\n  end\n  C->>V: render current local release immediately\n  C->>W: GET /v1/channels/delivery/stable (If-None-Match)\n  W-->>C: 304 or signed channel envelope\n\n  alt 304 / same release / keep-current\n    C-->>App: update event = no-update\n  else replay / invalid signature / expired / incompatible\n    C-->>App: structured rejection; keep current\n  else failed release ID\n    C-->>App: skipped-failed-release; keep current\n  else new eligible release\n    C->>R: GET immutable release envelope\n    C->>C: verify manifest hash + Ed25519\n    loop each declared file\n      C->>R: download immutable file to staging\n      C->>C: verify path + size + SHA-256\n    end\n    C->>S: atomic rename staging -> ready/releaseId\n\n    alt force=true or activation=on-launch\n      C->>S: previousLkg=active; attempting=releaseId\n      C->>V: reload verified local candidate\n      alt onLoad before watchdog\n        V-->>C: onLoad\n        C->>S: active=releaseId; clear attempting\n      else error or timeout\n        V-->>C: error/timeout\n        C->>S: failed+=releaseId; active=previousLkg\n        C->>V: render LKG or embedded\n      end\n    else activation=next-open\n      C->>S: pending=releaseId\n      C-->>App: update event = staged\n    end\n  end\n```\n\n### 4.2 Next-open activation\n\n```mermaid\nflowchart TD\n  A[App process starts] --> B{attemptingReleaseId exists?}\n  B -- yes --> C[Prior launch did not confirm]\n  C --> D[Mark failed + restore previous LKG]\n  B -- no --> E{pendingReleaseId exists and files valid?}\n  D --> E\n  E -- no --> F[Render active cache, else embedded]\n  E -- yes --> G[Set previousLkg = active]\n  G --> H[Set attempting = pending; clear pending]\n  H --> I[Render candidate before remote check]\n  I --> J{onLoad before watchdog?}\n  J -- yes --> K[Set active = candidate; clear attempting]\n  J -- no --> L[Mark failed; render previous LKG or embedded]\n  K --> M[Check channel once after first paint]\n  L --> M\n  F --> M\n```\n\n### 4.3 Result matrix\n\n| Condition | Device action | Visible result | Persistent state |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| First install, offline | Render embedded | Embedded UI | No remote active |\n| Cached active, offline | Render cached active | Last confirmed remote UI | State unchanged |\n| Server 304 / same release | No download | Current UI | Update `lastCheckedAt` |\n| New release, `next-open` | Verify + stage only | Current UI this launch | `pendingReleaseId = new` |\n| Next launch with pending | Attempt pending before check | New UI if load succeeds | Promote to active |\n| New release, `on-launch` | Verify + reload view | New UI this launch | Promote after `onLoad` |\n| Console `force=true` | Treat as `on-launch` | New UI after verification | Promote after `onLoad` |\n| Pointer signature invalid | Reject before manifest fetch | Current/LKG UI | Emit `signature` error |\n| Pointer revision replayed | Reject | Current/LKG UI | Keep highest revision |\n| Runtime incompatible | Reject before file download | Current/LKG UI | Emit `compatibility` |\n| Manifest hash/signature invalid | Reject | Current/LKG UI | Delete staging |\n| Any file size/hash mismatch | Reject transaction | Current/LKG UI | Delete staging |\n| Network failure | Stop check | Current/LKG or embedded UI | No activation change |\n| Candidate render error | Mark candidate failed; render prior | LKG/embedded UI | Restore active |\n| Candidate watchdog timeout | Same as render error | LKG/embedded UI | Restore active |\n| Process dies before confirmation | Detect next launch | LKG/embedded UI | Failed-history records candidate |\n| Server rollback to older release | Accept higher channel revision | Older release activates per policy | New target becomes active |\n| Rollback target already cached | Skip file download; re-verify stored envelope/files | Older UI faster | Active pointer changes |\n| Server returns failed release ID | Skip to prevent loop | Current/LKG UI | Failed history unchanged |\n| `keep-current` kill switch | No new download/activation | Current/LKG UI | State unchanged |\n\n---\n\n## 5. Require two taps for force/rollback: select action, then confirm exact release/version.\n4. Promote creates a new channel revision; rollback never mutates/deletes R2.\n5. “Force update” means `force=true` on a new signed pointer revision, not bypassing client safety.\n6. Record app build, Lynx SDK, runtimeVersion, channel revision, release ID, and platform for every run.\n2. Execute every row in Section 4.3 on iOS first.\n3. Hard stop: do not mark iOS PRs complete until real-device/simulator results are recorded.\n4. Execute the same rows on Android.\n5. Hard stop: do not merge Android parity until emulator/device evidence matches iOS.\n6. Run a tampered pointer, manifest, bundle, and sidecar test.\n7. Kill the process during staging and during candidate render.\n8. Test server rollback and force from the Access-protected console.\n9. Verify one active update transaction and bounded cache after repeated releases.\n10. Commit only test documentation/results; do not combine unverified platform work in one commit.\n\n---\n\n## 6. Risks and mitigations\n\n| Risk | Mitigation |\n|---|---|\n| Existing TS “stubs” become a second trust implementation | Delete/move them; native coordinator is authoritative |\n| Current diagram always renders embedded, causing flash/downgrade each launch | Render confirmed cache first; embedded only when no valid active cache exists |\n| Split-brain active pointer between file and preferences | One versioned preferences state; filesystem stores bytes/envelope only |\n| Signed old pointer replay blocks or downgrades devices | Monotonic channel revision; rollback uses a newer revision targeting an older release |\n| Key endpoint is mistaken for trust bootstrap | Embed public trust set in binary; remote key route is diagnostic/rotation support only |\n| Private key stored in D1 | Worker secret only; D1 stores key ID/public metadata at most |\n| Force update bricks users | Force changes activation timing only; all verification and fallback rules remain mandatory |\n| Candidate boot loop | `attemptingReleaseId` before render + next-launch recovery + failed ID blocklist |\n| Sidecar fetch after activation fails | Prefetch and verify every declared asset before promotion |\n| Cached release incompatible after app update | Exact runtimeVersion; fall back to embedded baseline after host update |\n| Multiple views race update downloads | One coordinator/task per feature and one serial store transaction |\n| Staging grows forever | Clean staging on startup and failure; bounded ready-directory prune policy |\n| Server rollback rejected as “older” | Compare channel revision, not semantic release version |\n| Hot Updater reuse adds thousands of unused lines | Port only crypto/preferences patterns; no archives/plugins/bsdiff |\n| Apple/Google OTA policy concern | Limit updates to Lynx UI/resources already supported by shipped native capabilities; document/store-review policy before production |\n\n---\n\n## 7. Open questions to settle before execution\n\nRecommended answers are shown first.\n\n1. **Server repo name/location:** use `expo-lynx-update-service` as a separate repo. Confirm the GitHub owner and local path before Task 15.\n2. **Default activation:** recommend `next-open`; `on-launch` is opt-in and console force overrides it for one revision.\n3. **Force behavior:** recommend non-blocking RN shell + verified current-launch Lynx activation; never show a hard update wall for a Lynx page.\n4. **Runtime version source:** recommend an explicit app-config string initially (for example `expo-lynx-1-lynx-4.0.0`), then automate fingerprinting only after the simple system ships.\n5. **Watchdog timeout:** recommend 10 seconds, configurable per app, not remotely controlled.\n6. **Web-console host:** recommend Cloudflare Pages/Worker static assets protected by Cloudflare Access.\n7. **Signing ownership:** recommend Worker signs after authenticated CI upload; alternatively CI signs and Worker only verifies/stores, but do not support both in v1.\n8. **Asset policy:** recommend all manifest-declared assets are mandatory and prefetched; optional/lazy assets are deferred.\n\n---\n\n## 8. Completion definition\n\nThe architecture is production-ready only when all are true:\n\n- The RN shell can always show either confirmed cached UI or embedded baseline offline.\n- Raw production URLs never reach Lynx.\n- Channel pointer, release manifest, and every file are authenticated/verified before activation.\n- `next-open`, `on-launch`, console force, and server rollback match the result matrix.\n- A broken or crashing immutable release cannot boot-loop a device.\n- The previous LKG is retained until the new candidate confirms.\n- All sidecar assets are available locally before the candidate is attempted.\n- One launch check and one update transaction exist per feature; no background timer exists.\n- iOS and Android pass the same real-device scenario matrix.\n- Server keys/secrets are stored correctly, admin operations are authenticated and audited, and rollback is one new channel revision.\n- Client PRs land in `release/bundle-update`; server PRs land in the separate service integration branch; neither goes directly to `main`.\n"}

{"content": "1|# Production architecture for Expo Lynx\n2|\n3|This directory describes the target production design for `expo-lynx`. The\n4|native host, rather than a caller-supplied URL, selects, verifies, caches, and\n5|rolls back executable Lynx bundles.\n6|\n7|## Documents\n8|\n9|- [Runtime architecture](./01-runtime-architecture.md)\n10|- [Bundle delivery](./02-bundle-delivery.md)\n11|- [Native module design](./03-native-module-design.md)\n12|- [Environment and security](./04-environment-security.md)\n13|- [Operations and verification](./05-operations-verification.md)\n14|- [Implementation plan](./06-implementation-plan.md)\n15|- [Known issues and fixes](./07-known-issues.md)\n16|- [Server update delivery](./08-server-update-delivery.md)\n17|- [Implementation spec](./09-implementation-spec.md)\n18|\n19|## Lynx engine runtime flow\n20|\n21|One path, top to bottom. **Start at ①, follow the arrows down.**\n22|\n23|```mermaid\n24|flowchart TD\n25|    A1[\"① ReactLynx source<br/>.tsx / .jsx\"]:::write\n26|    A2[\"② Bundle + template<br/>(built offline)\"]:::write\n27|    B1[\"③ JS engine<br/>PrimJS / V8 / JSC\"]:::run\n28|    B2[\"④ TASM<br/>template assembler\"]:::run\n29|    B3[\"⑤ Virtual DOM<br/>Element tree\"]:::run\n30|    B4[\"⑥ Starlight layout<br/>flex / CSS-like\"]:::run\n31|    B5[\"⑦ GFX + UI wrapper<br/>paints into native view\"]:::run\n32|    C1[\"⑧ Native View tree<br/>UIView / View\"]:::show\n33|    B6[\"⑨ Event bus<br/>gesture → JS callback\"]:::run\n34|\n35|    A1 --> A2 --> B1 --> B2 --> B3 --> B4 --> B5 --> C1\n36|    C1 -.tap.-> B6 -.calls back.-> B1\n37|\n38|    classDef write fill:#fff3bf,stroke:#1e1e1e,color:#1e1e1e\n39|    classDef run fill:#a5d8ff,stroke:#1e1e1e,color:#1e1e1e\n40|    classDef show fill:#b2f2bb,stroke:#1e1e1e,color:#1e1e1e\n41|```\n42|\n43|**Color legend:** yellow = you write it, blue = the engine runs it, green = the platform shows it.\n44|\n45|| # | What happens | Where it lives |\n46||---|-------------|----------------|\n47|| ① | You write `.tsx`. | Your editor. |\n48|| ② | Build step bundles JS + template. | Build pipeline (offline). |\n49|| ③ | Bundle loads into the JS engine, executes. | `core/runtime/js` |\n50|| ④ | JS calls into TASM to render components. | `core/renderer/tasm` |\n51|| ⑤ | TASM builds the virtual DOM. | `core/renderer/dom` |\n52|| ⑥ | Starlight measures & lays out the tree. | `core/renderer/starlight` |\n53|| ⑦ | GFX paints + UI wrapper maps to native view. | `gfx/`, `core/renderer/ui_wrapper` |\n54|| ⑧ | Native View tree displays on screen. | iOS / Android / Web shell |\n55|| ⑨ | User taps → event bus → JS callback → loop back to ③. | `core/event`, `core/renderer/events` |\n56|\n57|**The two arrows that always run:**\n58|\n59|- **Forward (①→⑧):** produce a frame on screen.\n60|- **Back (⑧→⑨→③):** user input loops back and triggers another forward pass.\n61|\n62|Debug surface (Inspector / Tracing) taps into the engine — it doesn't sit between steps.\n63|\n64|Editable hand-drawn version: [lynx-architecture.excalidraw](./lynx-architecture.excalidraw) (drag onto [excalidraw.com](https://excalidraw.com)).\n65|\n66|## Principles\n67|\n68|1. A Release build does not execute a bundle from an arbitrary React Native URL.\n69|2. Every app ships a known-good `static.lynx` fallback and its sidecar resources.\n70|3. A remote bundle must pass signature, compatibility, and hash validation.\n71|4. Updates activate only at a safe user-experience boundary.\n72|5. Keep a last-known-good version until its replacement renders successfully.\n73|\n74|The package is currently iOS-only. Android should implement the same source\n75|contract and bundle policy before it is advertised as supported.\n76|", "total_lines": 75, "file_size": 3450, "truncated": false, "is_binary": false, "is_image": false}

This changes only the selected pod\n45|targets (`Lynx`, `BaseDevtool`, `LynxDevtool`, and `LynxService`), not the\n46|React Native host target's build setting.\n47|\n48|**Validation**\n49|\n50|Run `pnpm expo prebuild --clean`, then build iOS. If it returns, inspect the\n51|generated Pods project and verify the setting is `YES` for those targets.\n52|\n53|## React Native native-binary mismatch\n54|\n55|**Message**\n56|\n57|```text\n58|TurboModuleRegistry.getEnforcing(...): 'NativeMicrotasksCxx' could not be found\n59|```\n60|\n61|**Status:** diagnostic; treat as an Expo/React Native native-binary issue.  \n62|**Scope:** React Native `0.86.2` / Expo native build, not the Lynx template.\n63|\n64|**Cause**\n65|\n66|The JavaScript bundle expects the React Native `NativeMicrotasksCxx` TurboModule\n67|but the installed iOS binary does not contain the matching RN runtime. This is\n68|typically a stale prebuild/Pods/app binary after an Expo or RN dependency change.\n69|\n70|**Fix**\n71|\n72|1. Ensure Expo and React Native versions match the Expo SDK's supported pair.\n73|2. Regenerate the iOS native project and Pods with `pnpm expo prebuild --clean`.\n74|3. Rebuild and reinstall the app; do not reuse an earlier simulator binary.\n75|4. Restart Metro with its cache cleared if the JavaScript bundle is stale.\n76|\n77|**Validation**\n78|\n79|Confirm the app no longer reports `NativeMicrotasksCxx` before investigating\n80|Lynx errors. The error occurs before the embedded view is useful.\n81|\n82|## LAN bundle server unavailable\n83|\n84|**Message**\n85|\n86|```text\n87|kCFErrorDomainCFNetwork error -1004\n88|NSURLErrorDomain -1004\n89|http://<LAN-IP>:<port>/main.lynx.bundle\n90|```\n91|\n92|**Status:** fixed by reachable development server configuration.  \n93|**Scope:** iOS networking and Rspeedy development server; not React Native or\n94|the Lynx bundle format.\n95|\n96|**Cause**\n97|\n98|The simulator/device could not connect to the server at the configured LAN IP\n99|and port. Common causes are a server bound only to loopback, an incorrect IP or\n100|port, firewall policy, or the device using a different network.\n101|\n102|**Fix**\n103|\n104|Start the Lynx source development server on a reachable interface, use its\n105|actual LAN IP in the example configuration, and allow local HTTP only for the\n106|Debug build's ATS policy. Check the exact URL from the simulator/device before\n107|opening the app.\n108|\n109|**Validation**\n110|\n111|`main.lynx.bundle` returns HTTP 200 from the simulator/device network path and\n112|the view's `onLoad` event fires.\n113|\n114|## HMR or live reload does not fetch updates\n115|\n116|**Message**\n117|\n118|```text\n119|The page reloads only after manual restart\n120|```\n121|\n122|**Status:** fixed for the current iOS Debug integration.  \n123|**Scope:** Lynx `4.0.0` embedded-host configuration.\n124|\n125|**Cause**\n126|\n127|Rspeedy update metadata and external JavaScript resources use Lynx's generic\n128|resource fetcher. A template fetcher alone can load `main.lynx.bundle` but does\n129|not fetch those hot-update resources. DevTool must also be configured before\n130|the views are created.\n131|\n132|**Fix**\n133|\n134|The current module prepares a global `LynxConfig` with\n135|`ExpoLynxTemplateProvider` before views are created, and each view configures\n136|the provider as its generic and media resource fetcher. See\n137|[ExpoLynxModule.swift](../ios/ExpoLynxModule.swift) and\n138|[ExpoLynxView.swift](../ios/ExpoLynxView.swift).\n139|\n140|**Important behavior**\n141|\n142|A Lynx template reload re-executes the page. It does not promise React-style\n143|Fast Refresh state preservation. Keep durable workflow state in React Native or\n144|the backend and pass it back through versioned `initialData` after a reload.\n145|\n146|**Validation**\n147|\n148|Save a Lynx source file, observe the update in the embedded view, then confirm\n149|the expected state is restored from the host rather than from the old template.\n150|\n151|## Static bundle renders briefly, then becomes blank\n152|\n153|**Message**\n154|\n155|```text\n156|Lynx error { code: '399', url: 'static.lynx' }\n157|```\n158|\n159|**Status:** fixed for the demo's static sidecar resources.  \n160|**Scope:** Lynx resource packaging; independent of React Native version.\n161|\n162|**Cause**\n163|\n164|`static.lynx` referenced images in `static/image/`, but shipping only the\n165|template omitted the bundle-relative resources from the iOS application bundle.\n166|\n167|**Fix**\n168|\n169|Bundle both `./assets/static.lynx` and `./assets/static` through the config\n170|plugin. The Release view keeps its generic/media resource pipeline enabled so\n171|the Lynx provider can resolve those files. See [example/app.json](../example/app.json)\n172|and [ExpoLynxView.swift](../ios/ExpoLynxView.swift).\n173|\n174|**Validation**\n175|\n176|Inspect the installed Release `.app`: it must contain `static.lynx` and every\n177|referenced image. The static screen must render with networking disabled.\n178|\n179|## Lynx Info logs appear in a Release build\n180|\n181|**Message**\n182|\n183|```text\n184|[lynx] [I:LynxEnv.mm(...)] LynxEnv: init success\n185|```\n186|\n187|**Status:** fixed in commit `fca885c`.  \n188|**Scope:** Lynx `4.0.0` iOS logging behavior, not React Native logging.\n189|\n190|**Cause**\n191|\n192|Lynx Release defaults native logging to `Info`; `LynxService/Log` routes those\n193|records to `NSLog`. Setting a threshold after `LynxEnv` is created is too late\n194|to suppress startup records.\n195|\n196|**Fix**\n197|\n198|Before `LynxEnv.sharedInstance()` runs, Release builds call:\n199|\n200|```swift\n201|SetMinimumLoggingLevel(.error)\n202|```\n203|\n204|This preserves error/fatal diagnostics. Lynx emits one expected setup line:\n205|\n206|```text\n207|W/lynx: Reset minimum log level as LynxLogLevelError\n208|```\n209|\n210|**Validation**\n211|\n212|Launch the Release app and exercise scrolling. No Lynx `INFO`, `DEBUG`, or\n213|normal interaction logs should appear after the threshold-reset line.\n214|\n215|## Deprecated React Native SafeAreaView\n216|\n217|**Message**\n218|\n219|```text\n220|SafeAreaView has been deprecated. {"path":"/Users/phirom/Desktop/expo-lynx/feature/delivery-bundle-update/README.md","content":"# Lynx bundle updates\n\nProduction delivery for a Lynx view embedded in Expo/React Native.\n\n## What it does\n\n1. Every app ships a working `static.lynx` baseline.\n2. At app launch, the native module renders the confirmed cached bundle, or the embedded baseline.\n3. It checks a signed Cloudflare channel pointer once.\n4. A new release downloads from R2 into staging with all declared assets.\n5. Native code verifies signatures, compatibility, file sizes, and SHA-256.\n6. The release activates now (`on-launch`) or on the next launch (`next-open`).\n7. A failed candidate rolls back to the previous last-known-good bundle.\n\nNo background timer. No mid-session swap. No arbitrary production URL from React Native.\n\n## Read these files\n\n| File | Read when |\n|---|---|\n| [ARCHITECTURE.md](./ARCHITECTURE.md) | Understand the complete runtime and Cloudflare flow |\n| [TESTING.md](./TESTING.md) | Verify implementation and production failure cases |\n| [ROADMAP.md](./ROADMAP.md) | See deliberately deferred work |\n| [`specs/`](./specs/) | Implementing or reviewing one ticket |\n\nYou normally need only this README and `ARCHITECTURE.md`.\n\n## Work order\n\nClient work lands in `release/bundle-update`, never directly in `main`.\n\n| Order | Spec | Result |\n|---:|---|---|\n| 1 | [Lynx source contract](./specs/client/pr-01-lynx-source.md) | `embedded`, `managed`, `development` sources |\n| 2 | [Release source guard](./specs/client/pr-02-release-source-guard.md) | Release rejects arbitrary URLs |\n| 3 | [Manifest verification](./specs/client/pr-03-manifest-sha256.md) | Bad bytes never reach Lynx |\n| 4 | logs](./specs/client/pr-10-release-log-hardening.md) | Error/Fatal only |\n| 11 | [DevTool split](./specs/client/pr-11-devtool-pod-split.md) | Debug tools absent from Release |\n| 12 | [Android patterns |\n\nServer contracts are mirrored under [`specs/server/`](./specs/server/) but land in a separate update-service repository.\n\n## PR contract\n\nThe first non-blank line of every PR body must be:\n\n```text\nSpec: feature/delivery-bundle-update/specs/client/pr-XX-name.md\n```\n\nThe AI reviewer reads that exact file and checks every acceptance criterion.\n\n## Hard rules\n\n- React {"content":"# Architecture\n\n## Goal\n\nEmbed Lynx as replaceable UI inside an Expo/React Native host while keeping production bundle delivery safe, offline-capable, and reversible.\n\n## System\n\n```mermaid\nflowchart TB\n  subgraph APP[Expo / React Native app]\n    RN[Feature screen\\nfeature + channel + initialData]\n    COORD[Native update coordinator]\n    STATE[UserDefaults / SharedPreferences\\nactive + previous + pending + failed]\n    STORE[Filesystem\\nstaging + verified releases]\n    VIEW[ExpoLynxView]\n    LYNX[Lynx engine]\n    BASE[Embedded baseline]\n\n    RN --> COORD\n    COORD --> STATE\n    COORD --> STORE\n    COORD --> VIEW --> LYNX\n    BASE --> STORE\n  end\n\n  subgraph CF[Cloudflare]\n    WORKER[Worker API]\n    D1[(D1\\nreleases + channel revisions)]\n    R2[(R2\\nimmutable bundles + assets)]\n    CONSOLE[Access-protected console\\npromote + force + rollback]\n\n    CONSOLE --> WORKER\n    WORKER --> D1\n    WORKER --> R2\n  end\n\n  COORD -- signed channel check --> WORKER\n  STORE -- immutable downloads --> R2\n```\n\n## Ownership\n\n| Component | Owns |\n|---|---|\n| React Native | Placement, feature/channel choice, durable workflow state, `initialData` |\n| Native coordinator | Update decision, activation, recovery, events |\n| Native state store | Active, previous LKG, pending, attempting, failed IDs |\n| Native bundle store | Staging, verification, atomic promote, pruning |\n| `ExpoLynxView` | Layout and rendering verified local URLs |\n| Worker + D1 | Mutable signed channel revision and audit history |\n| R2 | Immutable release manifest, bundle, and sidecar assets |\n\nReact Native never supplies an executable production URL. The CDN is not trusted without native verification.\n\n## App-launch flow\n\n```mermaid\nsequenceDiagram\n  autonumber\n  participant App as RN App\n  participant C as Native Coordinator\n  participant S as Local Store\n  participant V as LynxView\n  participant W as Worker\n  participant R as R2\n\n  App->>C: mount managed source\n  C->>S: recover unconfirmed candidate\n  C->>S: resolve active cache, else embedded\n  C->>V: render local bundle immediately\n  C->>W: GET signed channel pointer\n\n  alt no update / same release / 304\n    W-->>C: no change\n  else invalid or incompatible\n    C-->>App: reject; retain current UI\n  else new release\n    C->>R: fetch signed release manifest\n    C->>C: verify signature + runtimeVersion\n    C->>R: download bundle + every asset to staging\n    C->>C: verify path + size + SHA-256\n    C->>S: atomic promote to ready/releaseId\n\n    alt force or on-launch\n      C->>V: render candidate now\n      alt page loads before watchdog\n        C->>S: confirm candidate as active\n      else error or timeout\n        C->>S: mark failed + restore previous LKG\n        C->>V: render previous LKG or embedded\n      end\n    else next-open\n      C->>S: record pending candidate\n    end\n  end\n```\n\nThe channel is checked once per launch. There is no timer, OS background fetch, or mid-session swap.\n\n## Activation modes\n\n### `next-open` — default\n\n```text\nLaunch N\n  render current confirmed bundle\n  check channel\n  download + verify candidate and assets\n  save pendingReleaseId\n  keep current UI\n\nLaunch N+1\n  set attemptingReleaseId before render\n  render pending candidate\n  onLoad -> candidate becomes active/LKG\n  error, timeout, or process death -> roll back\n```\n\n### `on-launch`\n\n```text\nrender current confirmed bundle\ncheck channel\ncomplete download + verification\nset attemptingReleaseId\nreload LynxView with candidate\nonLoad -> candidate becomes active/LKG\nfailure -> restore previous LKG or embedded\n```\n\n### Console `force`\n\n`force=true` changes a verified candidate to current-launch activation. It does not bypass signature, runtime compatibility, SHA-256, crash history, or rollback. If the update cannot safely activate, the current UI remains available.\n\n## Local persistent state\n\nOne metadata store is authoritative; do not duplicate the active pointer in a separate text file.\n\n```json\n{\n  \"channel\": \"stable\",\n  \"lastAcceptedRevision\": 42,\n  \"activeReleaseId\": \"release-a\",\n  \"previousLkgReleaseId\": \"release-b\",\n  \"pendingReleaseId\": null,\n  \"attemptingReleaseId\": null,\n  \"failedReleaseIds\": [\"bad-release\"],\n  \"lastCheckedAt\": \"2026-08-28T01:20:00Z\",\n  \"lastETag\": \"...\"\n}\n```\n\nFilesystem:\n\n```text\n<Application Support>/ExpoLynx/delivery/\n  staging/<uuid>/\n  ready/<releaseId>/\n    release-envelope.json\n    main.lynx.bundle\n    static/...\n\nApp bundle:\n  static.lynx\n  static/...\n  embedded-release-envelope.json\n```\n\nOnly one update transaction runs at once. After successful activation, retain active + previous LKG; allow one pending candidate temporarily. Embedded baseline is never deleted.\n\n## Signed contracts\n\nUse a signed envelope so both clients verify the exact bytes instead of depending on JSON key order:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"payload\": \"base64url(UTF-8 JSON)\",\n  \"keyId\": \"k_2026_08\",\n  \"signature\": \"base64url(Ed25519 signature over decoded payload)\"\n}\n```\n\nChannel payload contains:\n\n- `feature`, `channel`\n- monotonic `revision`\n- target release ID, manifest URL, and manifest SHA-256\n- exact `runtimeVersion`\n- `activation: next-open | on-launch`\n- `force`\n- `issuedAt`, `expiresAt`\n\nA rollback creates a higher channel revision pointing to an older immutable release. Clients compare channel revision, not human version numbers, so rollback is accepted while replayed pointers are rejected.\n\nRelease payload contains:\n\n- release ID and display version\n- exact `runtimeVersion`\n- one template file\n- every sidecar asset with normalized relative path, immutable URL, byte count, and SHA-256\n\nAll files must verify before the staging directory is atomically renamed to `ready/<releaseId>`.\n\n## Cloudflare workflow\n\n```text\nCI build\n  -> produce production Lynx bundle + assets\n  -> POST authenticated release to Worker\n  -> Worker verifies hashes and signs manifest\n  -> Worker writes immutable objects to R2\n  -> Worker appends release metadata to D1\n\nOperator console\n  -> promote normally, force, or rollback\n  -> Worker creates channel revision N+1\n  -> Worker signs and stores the pointer\n\nDevice\n  -> GET /v1/channels/:feature/:channel\n  -> verify with public key embedded in app\n  -> download immutable release from R2\n```\n\nPrivate signing keys live only in Worker secrets. D1 stores release/channel metadata and signed pointer bytes, never private key material. The console uses Cloudflare Access instead of custom authentication.\n\n## Result matrix\n\n| Condition | Result |\n|---|---|\n| First install offline | Embedded baseline renders |\n| Confirmed cache offline | Cached active release renders |\n| Server says same release | No download |\n| New `next-open` release | Stage now; activate next launch |\n| New `on-launch` release | Activate after full verification this launch |\n| Console force | Same as verified `on-launch` |\n| Invalid pointer/manifest signature | Reject; keep current UI |\n| Replayed channel revision | Reject; keep current UI |\n| Wrong runtime version | Reject before file download |\n| File size/hash mismatch | Delete staging; keep current UI |\n| Candidate render error/timeout | Mark failed; restore previous LKG |\n| Process dies before candidate confirms | Recover next launch and restore LKG |\n| Server points to failed immutable ID | Skip to prevent boot loop |\n| Server rollback | Accept newer channel revision targeting older release |\n| Rollback target cached | Reuse verified local files |\n| Channel kill switch (`keep-current`) | Keep current UI and stop new activation |\n\n## Production rules\n\n- Always keep an embedded baseline compatible with the shipped Lynx SDK.\n- Keep durable session, navigation, form, and mutation state in React Native or the backend.\n- Release builds execute only embedded or verified local files.\n- Prefetch all declared assets before activation.\n- Public trust keys are embedded in the app; a key fetched from the update server cannot bootstrap trust.\n- Failed immutable release IDs stay blocked. Fixes must publish new bytes and therefore a new ID.\n- bsdiff, Sparkling, multi-feature routing, cohorts, and background downloads remain deferred until measured need exists.\n","path":"/Users/phirom/Desktop/expo-lynx/feature/delivery-bundle-update/ARCHITECTURE.md"}

{"content":"# Testing\n\n## Fast checks\n\n```bash\ncd /Users/phirom/Desktop/expo-lynx\npnpm run test\npnpm run lint\npnpm run build\n```\n\nThese prove the TypeScript surface and utilities compile. They do **not** prove native delivery, security, activation, or rollback.\n\n## Native build checks\n\n```bash\ncd /Users/phirom/Desktop/expo-lynx/example\npnpm expo prebuild --clean\n\n# iOS\ncd ios\npod install\nxcodebuild -list\n# Run the generated app workspace/scheme in Debug and Release.\n\n# Android\ncd ../android\n./gradlew test assembleDebug assembleRelease\n```\n\n## Required production matrix\n\nRecord platform, app build, Lynx SDK, runtime version, channel revision, and release ID for every run.\n\n| Scenario | Expected result |\n|---|---|\n| First install offline | Embedded baseline renders |\n| Confirmed cache offline | Cached active bundle renders |\n| Same release / HTTP 304 | No download or reload |\n| New release, `next-open` | Current UI remains; candidate activates next launch |\n| New release, `on-launch` | Candidate activates after verification this launch |\n| Console force | Same as verified `on-launch`; no safety bypass |\n| Invalid channel signature | Reject before manifest fetch |\n| Replayed channel revision | Reject and retain current release |\n| Invalid manifest signature/hash | Reject before activation |\n| Incompatible runtime version | Reject before file download |\n| Missing or bad sidecar | Delete staging; retain current UI |\n| Network interrupted during download | No partial release appears in `ready/` |\n| Two update checks race | One transaction wins; no duplicate/partial release |\n| Candidate render error | Previous LKG renders |\n| Candidate render timeout | Previous LKG renders |\n| Process killed before confirmation | Next launch recovers previous LKG |\n| Failed release returned again | Client skips it; no boot loop |\n| Server rollback | Older target activates from newer channel revision |\n| Cached rollback target | No redundant file download |\n| Kill switch (`keep-current`) | Current release remains active |\n| Release logs | No routine Lynx Debug/Info output |\n| Resource traversal path (`../`) | Manifest rejected |\n| Telemetry with token/query data | Sensitive content absent |\n\n## Completion gates\n\n- Run the full matrix on iOS before calling iOS complete.\n- Run the same matrix on Android before merging Android parity.\n- Do not combine an unverified platform with a verified platform in one completion claim.\n- Unit tests must include signed fixture vectors shared by TypeScript, Swift, Kotlin, and Worker.\n- A successful HTTP response is not success: read back R2/D1 state after publish, promote, force, and rollback.\n\n## Current status\n\nThe existing Jest tests cover provisional TypeScript contracts only. Native bundle storage, signature verification, Cloudflare delivery, activation, and rollback remain unverified until their platform tests and the matrix above pass.\n","path":"/Users/phirom/Desktop/expo-lynx/feature/delivery-bundle-update/TESTING.md"}

GET `/channels/:feature/:channel` (signed pointer, 60s cache)\n19|2. **Skip-check** against `crashHistory` in `LynxChannelState` (PR5). If the\n20|   server's manifest ID is in the crash history, do NOT download. Emit\n21|   `stage: 'crash_history'` and stop.\n22|3. Resolve `manifestUrl` from pointer\n23|4. Download manifest + verify Ed25519 signature with public key from `LynxEnvironment`\n24|5. Hand off to `LynxBundleStore` (PR5) for download.\n25|\n26|The crash-history skip prevents an infinite download loop: if v3 was tried\n27|last session and crashed before `notifyAppReady` fired (PR7's watchdog),\n28|the next session must not re-download v3.\n29|\n30|## Why\n31|\n32|See [Architecture](../../ARCHITECTURE.md).\n33|\n34|## Acceptance criteria\n35|\n36|- [ ] Tamper the manifest in R2 → client refuses, emits `stage: 'signature'`\n37|- [ ] Good manifest → proceeds to download\n38|- [ ] **A manifest ID in `crashHistory` is skipped without download**\n39|- [ ] Requires server PRs S1, S3, S4 deployed. Otherwise point at a stub URL that returns a hand-signed manifest for local testing.\n40|\n41|## Out of scope\n42|\n43|- Channel switching at runtime (separate concern)\n44|- LKG fallback (PR7)\n45|- `notifyAppReady` watchdog (PR7)\n46|", "total_lines": 45, "file_size": 1785, "truncated": false, "is_binary": false, "is_image": false}

Promote new candidate to `ready/<feature>/<vN>`.\n18|2. Render fails → revert render to `ready/<feature>/<vN-1>`.\n19|3. Delete `ready/<feature>/<vN>`.\n20|4. Telemetry: `stage: 'render'`, `source: 'cache'`.\n21|\n22|## Why\n23|\n24|See [Architecture](../../ARCHITECTURE.md).\n25|\n26|## Acceptance criteria\n27|\n28|- [ ] Push a candidate whose bundle crashes Lynx → app keeps showing v(N-1) with `onLoad` firing for v(N-1) instead of v(N)\n29|\n30|## Out of scope\n31|\n32|- Telemetry normalization (PR8)\n33|- Safe activation gating (PR9)\n34|", "total_lines": 33, "file_size": 906, "truncated": false, "is_binary": false, "is_image": false}

No background fetch, no\n8|mid-session swap. `on-launch` swaps in the same launch; `next-open` stages\n9|for the next launch.\n10|\n11|## Files\n12|\n13|- `ios/LynxBundleCoordinator.swift` (new — owns the launch sequence: render embedded → check → fetch → verify → stage → maybe-reload)\n14|- `example/App.tsx` (declare `activation` in `LynxSource`)\n15|\n16|## Contract\n17|\n18|```swift\n19|enum ActivationMode {\n20|    case onLaunch   // download + verify + reload in this launch\n21|    case nextOpen   // download + verify + stage; reload on next launch\n22|}\n23|\n24|func launchSequence(source: ManagedSource) async {\n25|    let embedded = renderEmbedded()           // always first; user sees something in <100ms\n26|    let server = try? await fetchChannel()\n27|    guard let server, server.manifestSha256 != local.last_manifest_id else { return }\n28|\n29|    let staged = try await downloadAndVerify(server)\n30|    switch source.activation {\n31|    case .onLaunch:  apply(staged)            // swap LynxView to staged\n32|    case .nextOpen:  return                    // staged sits in ready/<vN>, applied next launch\n33|    }\n34|}\n35|```\n36|\n37|## Why\n38|\n39|Mid-session updates are an anti-pattern: the user is mid-input, the\n40|bundle swaps underneath, state is lost or worse corrupted. Either\n41|update at launch (acceptable: first paint is the embedded baseline\n42|either way, so the user just sees the new bundle appear ~500ms later)\n43|or stage for next launch (acceptable: user reopens the app and sees\n44|the new bundle). Anything in between is trouble.\n45|\n46|## Acceptance criteria\n47|\n48|- [ ] `kind: 'managed', activation: 'on-launch'` → new bundle renders within the same launch (verified: device shows vN+1 after first launch with that mode)\n49|- [ ] `kind: 'managed', activation: 'next-open'` → first launch shows embedded baseline, kill app, relaunch → second launch shows vN+1\n50|- [ ] No activation happens while the user is interacting with the app\n51|- [ ] No background fetch — fetch is gated by `viewDidAppear` / `onResume`, not a timer\n52|- [ ] If `activation` is omitted from `LynxSource`, default to `'on-launch'` (matches Expo Updates behavior)\n53|\n54|## Out of scope\n55|\n56|- Mid-session swap with state preservation (deferred until someone asks)\n57|- Background prefetch on a timer (explicitly rejected)\n58|- Per-page activation mode (single mode per app, like Expo Updates)\n59|", "total_lines": 58, "file_size": 2453, "truncated": false, "is_binary": false, "is_image": false}

{"success": true, "name": "github-code-review", "description": "Review PRs: diffs, inline comments via gh or REST.", "tags": ["GitHub", "Code-Review", "Pull-Requests", "Git", "Quality"], "related_skills": ["github-auth", "github-pr-workflow"], "content": "---\nname: github-code-review\ndescription: \"Review PRs: diffs, inline comments via gh or REST.\"\nversion: 1.1.0\nauthor: Hermes Agent\nlicense: MIT\nplatforms: [linux, macos, windows]\nmetadata:\n  hermes:\n    tags: [GitHub, Code-Review, Pull-Requests, Git, Quality]\n    related_skills: [github-auth, github-pr-workflow]\n---\n\n# GitHub Code Review\n\nPerform code reviews on local changes before pushing, or review open PRs on GitHub. Most of this skill uses plain `git` — the `gh`/`curl` split only matters for PR-level interactions.\n\n## Prerequisites\n\n- Authenticated with GitHub (see `github-auth` skill)\n- Inside a git repository\n\n### Setup (for PR interactions)\n\n```bash\nif command -v gh &>/dev/null && gh auth status &>/dev/null; then\n  AUTH=\"gh\"\nelse\n  AUTH=\"git\"\n  if [ -z \"$GITHUB_TOKEN\" ]; then\n    if _hermes_env=\"${HERMES_HOME:-$HOME/.hermes}/.env\"; [ -f \"$_hermes_env\" ] && grep -q \"^GITHUB_TOKEN=\" \"$_hermes_env\"; then\n      GITHUB_TOKEN=$(grep \"^GITHUB_TOKEN=\" \"$_hermes_env\" | head -1 | cut -d= -f2 | tr -d '\\n\\r')\n    elif grep -q \"github.com\" ~/.git-credentials 2>/dev/null; then\n      GITHUB_TOKEN=$(uv run python \"${HERMES_HOME:-$HOME/.hermes}/skills/github/github-auth/scripts/git-credential-token.py\")\n    fi\n  fi\nfi\n\nREMOTE_URL=$(git remote get-url origin)\nOWNER_REPO=$(echo \"$REMOTE_URL\" | sed -E 's|.*github\\.com[:/]||; s|\\.git$||')\nOWNER=$(echo \"$OWNER_REPO\" | cut -d/ -f1)\nREPO=$(echo \"$OWNER_REPO\" | cut -d/ -f2)\n```\n\n---\n\n## 1. Reviewing Local Changes (Pre-Push)\n\nThis is pure `git` — works everywhere, no API needed.\n\n### Get the Diff\n\n```bash\n# Staged changes (what would be committed)\ngit diff --staged\n\n# All changes vs main (what a PR would contain)\ngit diff main...HEAD\n\n# File names only\ngit diff main...HEAD --name-only\n\n# Stat summary (insertions/deletions per file)\ngit diff main...HEAD --stat\n```\n\n### Review Strategy\n\n1. **Get the big picture first:**\n\n```bash\ngit diff main...HEAD --stat\ngit log main..HEAD --oneline\n```\n\n2. **Review file by file** — use `read_file` on changed files for full context, and the diff to see what changed:\n\n```bash\ngit diff main...HEAD -- src/auth/login.py\n```\n\n3. **Check for common issues:**\n\n```bash\n# Debug statements, TODOs, console.logs left behind\ngit diff main...HEAD | grep -n \"print(\\|console\\.log\\|TODO\\|FIXME\\|HACK\\|XXX\\|debugger\"\n\n# Large files accidentally staged\ngit diff main...HEAD --stat | sort -t'|' -k2 -rn | head -10\n\n# Secrets or credential patterns\ngit diff main...HEAD | grep -in \"password\\|secret\\|api_key\\|token.*=\\|private_key\"\n\n# Merge conflict markers\ngit diff main...HEAD | grep -n \"<<<<<<\\|>>>>>>\\|=======\"\n```\n\n4. **Present structured feedback** to the user.\n\n### Review Output Format\n\nWhen reviewing local changes, present findings in this structure:\n\n```\n## Code Review Summary\n\n### Critical\n- **src/auth.py:45** — SQL injection: user input passed directly to query.\n  Suggestion: Use parameterized queries.\n\n### Warnings\n- **src/models/user.py:23** — Password stored in plaintext. Use bcrypt or argon2.\n- **src/api/routes.py:112** — No rate limiting on login endpoint.\n\n### Suggestions\n- **src/utils/helpers.py:8** — Duplicates logic in `src/core/utils.py:34`. Consolidate.\n- **tests/test_auth.py** — Missing edge case: expired token test.\n\n### Looks Good\n- Clean separation of concerns in the middleware layer\n- Good test coverage for the happy path\n```\n\n---\n\n## 2. Reviewing a Pull Request on GitHub\n\n### View PR Details\n\n**With gh:**\n\n```bash\ngh pr view 123\ngh pr diff 123\ngh pr diff 123 --name-only\n```\n\n**With git + curl:**\n\n```bash\nPR_NUMBER=123\n\n# Get PR details\ncurl -s \\\n  -H \"Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN\" \\\n  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/pulls/$PR_NUMBER \\\n  | python -c \"\nimport sys, json\npr = json.load(sys.stdin)\nprint(f\\\"Title: {pr['title']}\\\")\nprint(f\\\"Author: {pr['user']['login']}\\\")\nprint(f\\\"Branch: {pr['head']['ref']} -> {pr['base']['ref']}\\\")\nprint(f\\\"State: {pr['state']}\\\")\nprint(f\\\"Body:\\n{pr['body']}\\\")\"\n\n# List changed files\ncurl -s \\\n  -H \"Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN\" \\\n  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/pulls/$PR_NUMBER/files \\\n  | python -c \"\nimport sys, json\nfor f in json.load(sys.stdin):\n    print(f\\\"{f['status']:10} +{f['additions']:-4} -{f['deletions']:-4}  {f['filename']}\\\")\"\n```\n\n### Check Out PR Locally for Full Review\n\nThis works with plain `git` — no `gh` needed:\n\n```bash\n# Fetch the PR branch and check it out\ngit fetch origin pull/123/head:pr-123\ngit checkout pr-123\n\n# Now you can use read_file, search_files, run tests, etc.\n\n# View diff against the base branch\ngit diff main...pr-123\n```\n\n**With gh (shortcut):**\n\n```bash\ngh pr checkout 123\n```\n\n### Leave Comments on a PR\n\n**General PR comment — with gh:**\n\n```bash\ngh pr comment 123 --body \"Overall looks good, a few suggestions below.\"\n```\n\n**General PR comment — with curl:**\n\n```bash\ncurl -s -X POST \\\n  -H \"Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN\" \\\n  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/issues/$PR_NUMBER/comments \\\n  -d '{\"body\": \"Overall looks good, a few suggestions below.\"}'\n```\n\n### Leave Inline Review Comments\n\n**Single inline comment — with gh (via API):**\n\n```bash\nHEAD_SHA=$(gh pr view 123 --json headRefOid --jq '.headRefOid')\n\ngh api repos/$OWNER/$REPO/pulls/123/comments \\\n  --method POST \\\n  -f body=\"This could be simplified with a list comprehension.\" \\\n  -f path=\"src/auth/login.py\" \\\n  -f commit_id=\"$HEAD_SHA\" \\\n  -f line=45 \\\n  -f side=\"RIGHT\"\n```\n\n**Single inline comment — with curl:**\n\n```bash\n# Get the head commit SHA\nHEAD_SHA=$(curl -s \\\n  -H \"Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN\" \\\n  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/pulls/$PR_NUMBER \\\n  | python -c \"import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin)['head']['sha'])\")\n\ncurl -s -X POST \\\n  -H \"Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN\" \\\n  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/pulls/$PR_NUMBER/comments \\\n  -d \"{\n    \\\"body\\\": \\\"This could be simplified with a list comprehension.\\\",\n    \\\"path\\\": \\\"src/auth/login.py\\\",\n    \\\"commit_id\\\": \\\"$HEAD_SHA\\\",\n    \\\"line\\\": 45,\n    \\\"side\\\": \\\"RIGHT\\\"\n  }\"\n```\n\n### Submit a Formal Review (Approve / Request Changes)\n\n**With gh:**\n\n```bash\ngh pr review 123 --approve --body \"LGTM!\"\ngh pr review 123 --request-changes --body \"See inline comments.\"\ngh pr review 123 --comment --body \"Some suggestions, nothing blocking.\"\n```\n\n**With curl — multi-comment review submitted atomically:**\n\n```bash\nHEAD_SHA=$(curl -s \\\n  -H \"Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN\" \\\n  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/pulls/$PR_NUMBER \\\n  | python -c \"import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin)['head']['sha'])\")\n\ncurl -s -X POST \\\n  -H \"Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN\" \\\n  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/pulls/$PR_NUMBER/reviews \\\n  -d \"{\n    \\\"commit_id\\\": \\\"$HEAD_SHA\\\",\n    \\\"event\\\": \\\"COMMENT\\\",\n    \\\"body\\\": \\\"Code review from Hermes Agent\\\",\n    \\\"comments\\\": [\n      {\\\"path\\\": \\\"src/auth.py\\\", \\\"line\\\": 45, \\\"body\\\": \\\"Use parameterized queries to prevent SQL injection.\\\"},\n      {\\\"path\\\": \\\"src/models/user.py\\\", \\\"line\\\": 23, \\\"body\\\": \\\"Hash passwords with bcrypt before storing.\\\"},\n      {\\\"path\\\": \\\"tests/test_auth.py\\\", \\\"line\\\": 1, \\\"body\\\": \\\"Add test for expired token edge case.\\\"}\n    ]\n  }\"\n```\n\nEvent values: `\"APPROVE\"`, `\"REQUEST_CHANGES\"`, `\"COMMENT\"`\n\nThe `line` field refers to the line number in the *new* version of the file. For deleted lines, use `\"side\": \"LEFT\"`.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Review Checklist\n\nWhen performing a code review (local or PR), systematically check:\n\n### Correctness\n- Does the code do what it claims?\n- Edge cases handled (empty inputs, nulls, large data, concurrent access)?\n- Error paths handled gracefully?\n\n### Security\n- No hardcoded secrets, credentials, or API keys\n- Input validation on user-facing inputs\n- No SQL injection, XSS, or path traversal\n- Auth/authz checks where needed\n\n### Code Quality\n- Clear naming (variables, functions, classes)\n- No unnecessary complexity or premature abstraction\n- DRY — no duplicated logic that should be extracted\n- Functions are focused (single responsibility)\n\n### Testing\n- New code paths tested?\n- Happy path and error cases covered?\n- Tests readable and maintainable?\n\n### Performance\n- No N+1 queries or unnecessary loops\n- Appropriate caching where beneficial\n- No blocking operations in async code paths\n\n### Documentation\n- Public APIs documented\n- Non-obvious logic has comments explaining \"why\"\n- README updated if behavior changed\n\n---\n\n## 4. Pre-Push Review Workflow\n\nWhen the user asks you to \"review the code\" or \"check before pushing\":\n\n1. `git diff main...HEAD --stat` — see scope of changes\n2. `git diff main...HEAD` — read the full diff\n3. For each changed file, use `read_file` if you need more context\n4. Apply the checklist above\n5. Present findings in the structured format (Critical / Warnings / Suggestions / Looks Good)\n6. If critical issues found, offer to fix them before the user pushes\n\n---\n\n## 5. PR Review Workflow (End-to-End)\n\nWhen the user asks you to \"review PR #N\", \"look at this PR\", or gives you a PR URL, follow this recipe:\n\n### Step 1: Set up environment\n\n```bash\nsource \"${HERMES_HOME:-$HOME/.hermes}/skills/github/github-auth/scripts/gh-env.sh\"\n# Or run the inline setup block from the top of this skill\n```\n\n### Step 2: Gather PR context\n\nGet the PR metadata, description, and list of changed files to understand scope before diving into code.\n\n**With gh:**\n```bash\ngh pr view 123\ngh pr diff 123 --name-only\ngh pr checks 123\n```\n\n**With curl:**\n```bash\nPR_NUMBER=123\n\n# PR details (title, author, description, branch)\ncurl -s -H \"Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN\" \\\n  https://api.github.com/repos/$GH_OWNER/$GH_REPO/pulls/$PR_NUMBER\n\n# Changed files with line counts\ncurl -s -H \"Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN\" \\\n  https://api.github.com/repos/$GH_OWNER/$GH_REPO/pulls/$PR_NUMBER/files\n```\n\n### Step 2a: Resolve the spec (if present)\n\nIf the repo uses feature specs (look for `feature/**/README.md` or a\n`lynx-architecture/` folder), the PR body's first non-blank line may\nbegin with `Spec: <path>`. Treat that as mandatory:\n\n```bash\n# Extract the Spec: link from PR body\nSPEC_PATH=$(gh pr view 123 --json body --jq -r '.body' | head -1 | sed -n 's/^Spec:[[:space:]]*//p')\n\nif [ -n \"$SPEC_PATH\" ]; then\n  # Resolve relative to repo root\n  REPO_ROOT=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)\n  SPEC_FILE=\"$REPO_ROOT/$SPEC_PATH\"\n\n  if [ -f \"$SPEC_FILE\" ]; then\n    # Read the spec — its Acceptance Criteria section is what to compare against\n    cat \"$SPEC_FILE\"\n  else\n    echo \"REJECT: spec file not found: $SPEC_PATH\"\n    exit 1\n  fi\nfi\n```\n\n**Hard rule:** if `Spec:` line is missing in a repo that uses specs, or\npoints at a file that doesn't exist, post a single comment and stop:\n\n```\n❌ Cannot review: PR body is missing `Spec: <path>` on the first line,\nor that file does not exist at the repo root. See <feature-folder>/README.md\nfor the required PR template.\n```\n\nUse `event: REQUEST_CHANGES` with that body. Don't attempt review without\na spec — every review here is *spec vs. diff*, not *style vs. diff*.\n\n### Step 3: Check out the PR locally\n\nThis gives you full access to `read_file`, `search_files`, and the ability to run tests.\n\n```bash\ngit fetch origin pull/$PR_NUMBER/head:pr-$PR_NUMBER\ngit checkout pr-$PR_NUMBER\n```\n\n### Step 4: Read the diff and understand changes\n\n```bash\n# Full diff against the base branch\ngit diff main...HEAD\n\n# Or file-by-file for large PRs\ngit diff main...HEAD --name-only\n# Then for each file:\ngit diff main...HEAD -- path/to/file.py\n```\n\nFor each changed file, use `read_file` to see full context around the changes — diffs alone can miss issues visible only with surrounding code.\n\n### Step 5: Compare against spec acceptance criteria\n\nIf a spec was resolved in Step 2a, walk through every checkbox under the\nspec's \"Acceptance criteria\" section. For each:\n\n- **Pass:** the diff includes the code that satisfies it. Cite file:line.\n- **Fail:** the diff is missing it, or contradicts it. Cite spec section\n  + diff evidence. This is an inline comment, severity 🔴.\n- **Unverifiable from diff:** e.g. \"real-device test on iOS\" — note as\n  ⚠ in the summary, do NOT block merge on it.\n\n### Step 6: Run automated checks locally (if applicable)\n\n```bash\n# Run tests if there's a test suite\npython -m pytest 2>&1 | tail -20\n# or: npm test, cargo test, go test ./...\n\n# Run linter if configured\nruff check . 2>&1 | head -30\n# or: eslint, clippy, ...\n```\n\n### Step 7: Apply the review checklist (Section 3)\n\nGo through each category: Correctness, Security, Code Quality, Testing, Performance, Documentation.\n\nSpec-driven findings (Step 5) outrank style findings (Step 7). A PR that\nmatches its spec but has a style nit is ✅. A PR that doesn't match its\nspec is ❌ regardless of style.\n\n### Step 8: Post the review to GitHub\n\nCollect your findings and submit them as a formal review with inline comments.\n\n**With gh:**\n```bash\n# If no issues — approve\ngh pr review $PR_NUMBER --approve --body \"Reviewed by Hermes Agent. Code looks clean — good test coverage, no security concerns.\"\n\n# If issues found — request changes with inline comments\ngh pr review $PR_NUMBER --request-changes --body \"Found a few issues — see inline comments.\"\n```\n\n**With curl — atomic review with multiple inline comments:**\n```bash\nHEAD_SHA=$(curl -s -H \"Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN\" \\\n  https://api.github.com/repos/$GH_OWNER/$GH_REPO/pulls/$PR_NUMBER \\\n  | python -c \"import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin)['head']['sha'])\")\n\n# Build the review JSON — event is APPROVE, REQUEST_CHANGES, or COMMENT\ncurl -s -X POST \\\n  -H \"Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN\" \\\n  https://api.github.com/repos/$GH_OWNER/$GH_REPO/pulls/$PR_NUMBER/reviews \\\n  -d \"{\n    \\\"commit_id\\\": \\\"$HEAD_SHA\\\",\n    \\\"event\\\": \\\"REQUEST_CHANGES\\\",\n    \\\"body\\\": \\\"## Hermes Agent Review\\n\\nFound 2 issues, 1 suggestion. See inline comments.\\\",\n    \\\"comments\\\": [\n      {\\\"path\\\": \\\"src/auth.py\\\", \\\"line\\\": 45, \\\"body\\\": \\\"🔴 **Critical:** User input passed directly to SQL query — use parameterized queries.\\\"},\n      {\\\"path\\\": \\\"src/models.py\\\", \\\"line\\\": 23, \\\"body\\\": \\\"⚠️ **Warning:** Password stored without hashing.\\\"},\n      {\\\"path\\\": \\\"src/utils.py\\\", \\\"line\\\": 8, \\\"body\\\": \\\"💡 **Suggestion:** This duplicates logic in core/utils.py:34.\\\"}\n    ]\n  }\"\n```\n\n### Step 8: Also post a summary comment\n\nIn addition to inline comments, leave a top-level summary so the PR author gets the full picture at a glance. Use the review output format from `references/review-output-template.md`.\n\nWhen a spec was resolved in Step 2a, the summary MUST include a spec-compliance block:\n\n```markdown\n## Code Review Summary\n\n**Verdict: Changes Requested** (2 issues, 1 suggestion)\n\n### Spec compliance (feature/delivery-bundle-update/pr-03-manifest-sha256.md)\n- ✅ Manifest types match `src/manifest.ts` exactly.\n- ✅ SHA-256 check fires before `lynxView.loadTemplate` (ExpoLynxView.swift:340).\n- ❌ Manifest `signature` field is parsed but not verified — spec lists signature verification as OUT OF SCOPE for PR3, but the PR is also missing the explicit comment that defers it. Add a one-line comment.\n\n### 🔴 Critical\n- **src/auth.py:45** — SQL injection vulnerability\n\n### ⚠️ Warnings\n- **src/models.py:23** — Plaintext password storage\n\n### 💡 Suggestions\n- **src/utils.py:8** — Duplicated logic, consider consolidating\n\n### ✅ Looks Good\n- Clean API design\n- Good error handling in the middleware layer\n```\n\nThe spec-compliance block is non-negotiable when a spec is present. A reviewer that omits it has not actually done the review.\n\n**With gh:**\n```bash\ngh pr comment $PR_NUMBER --body \"$(cat <<'EOF'\n## Code Review Summary\n\n**Verdict: Changes Requested** (2 issues, 1 suggestion)\n\n### 🔴 Critical\n- **src/auth.py:45** — SQL injection vulnerability\n\n### ⚠️ Warnings\n- **src/models.py:23** — Plaintext password storage\n\n### 💡 Suggestions\n- **src/utils.py:8** — Duplicated logic, consider consolidating\n\n### ✅ Looks Good\n- Clean API design\n- Good error handling in the middleware layer\n\n---\n*Reviewed by Hermes Agent*\nEOF\n)\"\n```\n\n### Step 9: Clean up\n\n```bash\ngit checkout main\ngit branch -D pr-$PR_NUMBER\n```\n\n### Decision: Approve vs Request Changes vs Comment\n\n- **Approve** — spec-compliance is ✅ for every criterion, AND no critical\n  or warning-level issues from the standard checklist.\n- **Request Changes** — any spec-compliance ❌ OR any critical issue.\n  Even one missing acceptance criterion is enough.\n- **Comment** — observations and suggestions, but nothing blocking (use\n  when you're unsure or the PR is a draft).\n\n### Step 9: Clean up\n\n```bash\ngit checkout main\ngit branch -D pr-$PR_NUMBER\n```\n", "path": "github/github-code-review/SKILL.md", "skill_dir": "/Users/phirom/.hermes/skills/github/github-code-review", "org_provenance": null, "linked_files": {"success": true, "name": "github-issues", "description": "Create, triage, label, assign GitHub issues via gh or REST.", "tags": ["GitHub", "Issues", "Project-Management", "Bug-Tracking", "Triage"], "related_skills": ["github-auth", "github-pr-workflow"], "content": "---\nname: github-issues\ndescription: \"Create, triage, label, assign GitHub issues via gh or REST.\"\nversion: 1.1.0\nauthor: Hermes Agent\nlicense: MIT\nplatforms: [linux, macos, windows]\nmetadata:\n  hermes:\n    tags: [GitHub, Issues, Project-Management, Bug-Tracking, Triage]\n    related_skills: [github-auth, github-pr-workflow]\n---\n\n# GitHub Issues Management\n\nCreate, search, triage, and manage GitHub issues. Each section shows `gh` first, then the `curl` fallback.\n\n## Prerequisites\n\n- Authenticated with GitHub (see `github-auth` skill)\n- Inside a git repo with a GitHub remote, or specify the repo explicitly\n\n### Setup\n\n```bash\nif command -v gh &>/dev/null && gh auth status &>/dev/null; then\n  AUTH=\"gh\"\nelse\n  AUTH=\"git\"\n  if [ -z \"$GITHUB_TOKEN\" ]; then\n    if _hermes_env=\"${HERMES_HOME:-$HOME/.hermes}/.env\"; [ -f \"$_hermes_env\" ] && grep -q \"^GITHUB_TOKEN=\" \"$_hermes_env\"; then\n      GITHUB_TOKEN=$(grep \"^GITHUB_TOKEN=\" \"$_hermes_env\" | head -1 | cut -d= -f2 | tr -d '\\n\\r')\n    elif grep -q \"github.com\" ~/.git-credentials 2>/dev/null; then\n      GITHUB_TOKEN=$(uv run python \"${HERMES_HOME:-$HOME/.hermes}/skills/github/github-auth/scripts/git-credential-token.py\")\n    fi\n  fi\nfi\n\nREMOTE_URL=$(git remote get-url origin)\nOWNER_REPO=$(echo \"$REMOTE_URL\" | sed -E 's|.*github\\.com[:/]||; s|\\.git$||')\nOWNER=$(echo \"$OWNER_REPO\" | cut -d/ -f1)\nREPO=$(echo \"$OWNER_REPO\" | cut -d/ -f2)\n```\n\n---\n\n## 1. Viewing Issues\n\n**With gh:**\n\n```bash\ngh issue list\ngh issue list --state open --label \"bug\"\ngh issue list --assignee @me\ngh issue list --search \"authentication error\" --state all\ngh issue view 42\n```\n\n**With curl:**\n\n```bash\n# List open issues\ncurl -s \\\n  -H \"Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN\" \\\n  \"https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/issues?state=open&per_page=20\" \\\n  | python -c \"\nimport sys, json\nfor i in json.load(sys.stdin):\n    if 'pull_request' not in i:  # GitHub API returns PRs in /issues too\n        labels = ', '.join(l['name'] for l in i['labels'])\n        print(f\\\"#{i['number']:5}  {i['state']:6}  {labels:30}  {i['title']}\\\")\"\n\n# Filter by label\ncurl -s \\\n  -H \"Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN\" \\\n  \"https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/issues?state=open&labels=bug&per_page=20\" \\\n  | python -c \"\nimport sys, json\nfor i in json.load(sys.stdin):\n    if 'pull_request' not in i:\n        print(f\\\"#{i['number']}  {i['title']}\\\")\"\n\n# View a specific issue\ncurl -s \\\n  -H \"Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN\" \\\n  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/issues/42 \\\n  | python -c \"\nimport sys, json\ni = json.load(sys.stdin)\nlabels = ', '.join(l['name'] for l in i['labels'])\nassignees = ', '.join(a['login'] for a in i['assignees'])\nprint(f\\\"#{i['number']}: {i['title']}\\\")\nprint(f\\\"State: {i['state']}  Labels: {labels}  Assignees: {assignees}\\\")\nprint(f\\\"Author: {i['user']['login']}  Created: {i['created_at']}\\\")\nprint(f\\\"\\n{i['body']}\\\")\"\n\n# Search issues\ncurl -s \\\n  -H \"Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN\" \\\n  \"https://api.github.com/search/issues?q=authentication+error+repo:$OWNER/$REPO\" \\\n  | python -c \"\nimport sys, json\nfor i in json.load(sys.stdin)['items']:\n    print(f\\\"#{i['number']}  {i['state']:6}  {i['title']}\\\")\"\n```\n\n## 2. Creating Issues\n\n**With gh:**\n\n```bash\ngh issue create \\\n  --title \"Login redirect ignores ?next= parameter\" \\\n  --body \"## Description\nAfter logging in, users always land on /dashboard.\n\n## Steps to Reproduce\n1. Navigate to /settings while logged out\n2. Get redirected to /login?next=/settings\n3. Log in\n4. Actual: redirected to /dashboard (should go to /settings)\n\n## Expected Behavior\nRespect the ?next= query parameter.\" \\\n  --label \"bug,backend\" \\\n  --assignee \"username\"\n```\n\n**With curl:**\n\n```bash\ncurl -s -X POST \\\n  -H \"Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN\" \\\n  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/issues \\\n  -d '{\n    \"title\": \"Login redirect ignores ?next= parameter\",\n    \"body\": \"## Description\\nAfter logging in, users always land on /dashboard.\\n\\n## Steps to Reproduce\\n1. Navigate to /settings while logged out\\n2. Get redirected to /login?next=/settings\\n3. Log in\\n4. Actual: redirected to /dashboard\\n\\n## Expected Behavior\\nRespect the ?next= query parameter.\",\n    \"labels\": [\"bug\", \"backend\"],\n    \"assignees\": [\"username\"]\n  }'\n```\n\n### Bug Report Template\n\n```\n## Bug Description\n<What's happening>\n\n## Steps to Reproduce\n1. <step>\n2. <step>\n\n## Expected Behavior\n<What should happen>\n\n## Actual Behavior\n<What actually happens>\n\n## Environment\n- OS: <os>\n- Version: <version>\n```\n\n### Feature Request Template\n\n```\n## Feature Description\n<What you want>\n\n## Motivation\n<Why this would be useful>\n\n## Proposed Solution\n<How it could work>\n\n## Alternatives Considered\n<Other approaches>\n```\n\n## 3. Managing Issues\n\n### Add/Remove Labels\n\n**With gh:**\n\n```bash\ngh issue edit 42 --add-label \"priority:high,bug\"\ngh issue edit 42 --remove-label \"needs-triage\"\n```\n\n**With curl:**\n\n```bash\n# Add labels\ncurl -s -X POST \\\n  -H \"Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN\" \\\n  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/issues/42/labels \\\n  -d '{\"labels\": [\"priority:high\", \"bug\"]}'\n\n# Remove a label\ncurl -s -X DELETE \\\n  -H \"Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN\" \\\n  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/issues/42/labels/needs-triage\n\n# List available labels in the repo\ncurl -s \\\n  -H \"Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN\" \\\n  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/labels \\\n  | python -c \"\nimport sys, json\nfor l in json.load(sys.stdin):\n    print(f\\\"  {l['name']:30}  {l.get('description', '')}\\\")\"\n```\n\n### Assignment\n\n**With gh:**\n\n```bash\ngh issue edit 42 --add-assignee username\ngh issue edit 42 --add-assignee @me\n```\n\n**With curl:**\n\n```bash\ncurl -s -X POST \\\n  -H \"Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN\" \\\n  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/issues/42/assignees \\\n  -d '{\"assignees\": [\"username\"]}'\n```\n\n### Commenting\n\n**With gh:**\n\n```bash\ngh issue comment 42 --body \"Investigated — root cause is in auth middleware. Working on a fix.\"\n```\n\n**With curl:**\n\n```bash\ncurl -s -X POST \\\n  -H \"Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN\" \\\n  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/issues/42/comments \\\n  -d '{\"body\": \"Investigated — root cause is in auth middleware. Working on a fix.\"}'\n```\n\n### Closing and Reopening\n\n**With gh:**\n\n```bash\ngh issue close 42\ngh issue close 42 --reason \"not planned\"\ngh issue reopen 42\n```\n\n**With curl:**\n\n```bash\n# Close\ncurl -s -X PATCH \\\n  -H \"Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN\" \\\n  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/issues/42 \\\n  -d '{\"state\": \"closed\", \"state_reason\": \"completed\"}'\n\n# Reopen\ncurl -s -X PATCH \\\n  -H \"Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN\" \\\n  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/issues/42 \\\n  -d '{\"state\": \"open\"}'\n```\n\n### Linking Issues to PRs\n\nIssues are automatically closed when a PR merges with the right keywords in the body:\n\n```\nCloses #42\nFixes #42\nResolves #42\n```\n\nTo create a branch from an issue:\n\n**With gh:**\n\n```bash\ngh issue develop 42 --checkout\n```\n\n**With git (manual equivalent):**\n\n```bash\ngit checkout main && git pull origin main\ngit checkout -b fix/issue-42-login-redirect\n```\n\n## 4. Issue Triage Workflow\n\nWhen asked to triage issues:\n\n1. **List untriaged issues:**\n\n```bash\n# With gh\ngh issue list --label \"needs-triage\" --state open\n\n# With curl\ncurl -s \\\n  -H \"Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN\" \\\n  \"https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/issues?labels=needs-triage&state=open\" \\\n  | python -c \"\nimport sys, json\nfor i in json.load(sys.stdin):\n    if 'pull_request' not in i:\n        print(f\\\"#{i['number']}  {i['title']}\\\")\"\n```\n\n2. **Read and categorize** each issue (view details, understand the bug/feature)\n\n3. **Apply labels and priority** (see Managing Issues above)\n\n4. **Assign** if the owner is clear\n\n5. **Comment with triage notes** if needed\n\n## 5. Bulk Operations\n\nFor batch operations, combine API calls with shell scripting:\n\n**With gh:**\n\n```bash\n# Close all issues with a specific label\ngh issue list --label \"wontfix\" --json number --jq '.[].number' | \\\n  xargs -I {} gh issue close {} --reason \"not planned\"\n```\n\n**With curl:**\n\n```bash\n# List issue numbers with a label, then close each\ncurl -s \\\n  -H \"Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN\" \\\n  \"https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/issues?labels=wontfix&state=open\" \\\n  | python -c \"import sys,json; [print(i['number']) for i in json.load(sys.stdin)]\" \\\n  | while read num; do\n    curl -s -X PATCH \\\n      -H \"Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN\" \\\n      https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/issues/$num \\\n      -d '{\"state\": \"closed\", \"state_reason\": \"not_planned\"}'\n    echo \"Closed #$num\"\n  done\n```\n\n## Quick Reference Table\n\n| Action | gh | curl endpoint |\n|--------|-----|--------------|\n| List issues | `gh issue list` | `GET /repos/{o}/{r}/issues` |\n| View issue | `gh issue view N` | `GET /repos/{o}/{r}/issues/N` |\n| Create issue | `gh issue create ...` | `POST /repos/{o}/{r}/issues` |\n| Add labels | `gh issue edit N --add-label ...` | `POST /repos/{o}/{r}/issues/N/labels` |\n| Assign | `gh issue edit N --add-assignee ...` | `POST /repos/{o}/{r}/issues/N/assignees` |\n| Comment | `gh issue comment N --body ...` | `POST /repos/{o}/{r}/issues/N/comments` |\n| Close | `gh issue close N` | `PATCH /repos/{o}/{r}/issues/N` |\n| Search | `gh issue list --search \"...\"` | `GET /search/issues?q=...` |\n", "path": "github/github-issues/SKILL.md", "skill_dir": "/Users/phirom/.hermes/skills/github/github-issues", "org_provenance": null, "linked_files": {"templates": ["templates/feature-request.md", "templates/bug-report.md"]}, "usage_hint": "To view linked files, call skill_view(name, file_path) where file_path is e.g. 'references/api.md' or 'assets/config.yaml'", "required_environment_variables": [], "required_commands": [], "missing_required_environment_variables": [], "missing_credential_files": [], "missing_required_commands": [], "setup_needed": false, "setup_skipped": false, "readiness_status": "available", "_source_path": "/Users/phirom/.hermes/skills/github/github-issues/SKILL.md", "metadata": {"hermes": {"tags": ["GitHub", "Issues", "Project-Management", "Bug-Tracking", "Triage"], "related_skills": ["github-auth", "github-pr-workflow"]}}}
